questions.prompt: The Common Closure Principle (CCP) is essentially which class-level principle, applied to components?

options.text: The Single Responsibility Principle (group classes that change for the same reasons)

questions.explanation: CCP is SRP for components: gather classes that change for the same reasons and at the same times, so a change touches as few components as possible.

questions.prompt: Given instability I = Ce/(Ca+Ce), order these components from MOST stable to MOST unstable.
questions.explanation: Lower instability means more stable. I = 0 is maximally stable (much depends on it, it depends on nothing); dependencies should point from higher-I toward lower-I components.

questions.prompt: The Acyclic Dependencies Principle says the component dependency graph must contain no ______.
questions.explanation: The component graph must be a directed acyclic graph (DAG). Break a cycle with DIP or by extracting a new component.

questions.prompt: Which are valid ways to break a dependency cycle in the component graph? Select all that apply.

options.text: Apply DIP — invert one dependency with an interface
Extract a new component that both cyclic components depend on
Add another dependency to complete the loop
Permanently merge everything into one giant component

questions.explanation: Inverting a dependency (DIP) or extracting a shared component restores an acyclic graph (ADP). Adding dependencies or merging everything does not properly break the cycle.

questions.prompt: Match each component principle acronym to its idea.

pairs.right: The granule of reuse is the granule of release
Don't force clients to depend on classes they don't use
Depend in the direction of stability
A component's abstractness should match its stability

questions.explanation: REP/CCP/CRP are the cohesion principles; ADP/SDP/SAP are the coupling principles. SDP + SAP mean stable components should be abstract.

questions.prompt: A concrete 'common' package (A ≈ 0) that everything depends on (I ≈ 0) sits in which zone?

options.text: The Zone of Pain — stable and concrete, rigid but heavily depended on
The Zone of Uselessness — abstract and unstable

questions.explanation: Low abstractness + low instability is the Zone of Pain: rigid yet universally depended upon. SAP says such a stable component should be abstract so it can be extended.
